stories.original:
**Visa shuts down US open banking unit amid regulatory uncertainty**

*Visa has closed its US open banking operation, a direct consequence of the regulatory limbo surrounding the CFPB's rewritten data-sharing rule.*

Visa's decision to wind down the US open banking unit it built through its 2020 acquisition of Plaid (after the original merger was blocked) marks a significant retreat. The closure follows months of uncertainty over the scope and enforceability of the CFPB's open banking rule, which was substantially narrowed in June under the current administration.

The move raises questions about the viability of network-led open banking strategies in a market where the regulatory framework remains unsettled. Visa had positioned the unit as a bridge between its card network and account-to-account data flows, but without a clear federal mandate for data sharing, the commercial case evidently weakened.

For European observers, the contrast is instructive. PSD2 and its successors have created a regulatory baseline that, whatever its shortcomings, provides enough certainty for investment. The US continues to lack that foundation, and Visa's exit suggests even well-capitalised incumbents are unwilling to build on shifting ground.

*Sources: [Visa pulls plug on U.S. open banking arm amid regulator uncertainty](http://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/visa-pulls-plug-on-us-open-banking-arm-amid-regulator-uncertainty-report/ar-AA1L28id) — MSN*

**FCA publishes AI review with open finance and agentic payments in scope**

*The FCA's Mills Review sets out how AI could reshape UK retail financial services by 2030, with recommendations spanning open finance powers and agentic AI oversight.*

The FCA has published a wide-ranging review, led by external adviser Mills, examining how AI will transform retail financial services and what regulatory responses are needed. The review recommends that the FCA seek explicit powers over open finance and addresses how existing regulatory frameworks apply to early agentic AI use cases in payments and advice.

According to The Banker's reporting on an exclusive interview with FCA officials, the regulator believes its current powers are sufficient to oversee early-stage agentic AI but acknowledges gaps around open finance infrastructure. The FCA appears to be positioning itself as the natural regulator for the data-sharing layer that underpins agentic payments, building on its existing open banking remit.

The review lands at a moment when agentic payments are moving from proof of concept to early production in Europe, with Crédit Agricole, ING and Visa all completing live transactions in recent weeks. The FCA's willingness to assert jurisdiction over the intersection of AI and open finance signals that regulatory frameworks will need to evolve quickly to keep pace.

*Sources: [FCA publishes landmark review into impact of AI on retail financial services](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/fca-publishes-landmark-review-impact-ai-retail-financial-services) — FCA | [AI and the future of retail financial services (The Mills Review)](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/corporate-documents/mills-review) — FCA | [Existing rules can police early agentic AI, says UK watchdog](https://www.thebanker.com/content/c32b69a6-f8ac-4067-a03c-7756194cd78c) — The Banker*

**Montenegro to launch instant payments on July 20 using SEPA standards**

*Montenegro will go live with domestic instant payments later this month, adopting SEPA standards despite not being an EU member state.*

Montenegro's central bank has confirmed that the country's instant payment service will launch on July 20, making it one of the first Western Balkan states to implement real-time payments infrastructure built to SEPA standards. The system will initially support domestic transfers, with cross-border connectivity expected to follow.

The decision to build on SEPA standards rather than a proprietary domestic system reflects a broader pattern among EU accession candidates aligning their financial infrastructure with European norms ahead of membership. Iceland's recent connection to TIPS followed similar logic, extending euro-area payment rails beyond the eurozone's formal borders.

For the instant payments ecosystem, each new market adopting SEPA-compatible infrastructure widens the addressable network and reinforces the interoperability logic underpinning the EU's instant payments regulation.

*Sources: [Montenegro ready for July 20 instant payment service launch](https://seenews.com/news/montenegro-ready-for-july-20-instant-payment-service-launch-1297571) — SeeNews*

**Canada publishes draft consumer-driven banking regulations**

*Canada has released draft regulations for its consumer-driven banking framework, moving one of the last major Western economies closer to a formal open banking regime.*

The Canadian government has published proposed consumer-driven banking regulations for public comment, a concrete step after years of consultation and legislative groundwork. The draft rules establish the framework for how banks and accredited third parties will share consumer financial data, with potential extension to insurance and investment products.

Canada's approach draws on lessons from both the UK's open banking mandate and Australia's Consumer Data Right, though it has moved more slowly than either. The publication of draft regulations rather than high-level principles signals that the framework is approaching implementation, though the comment period and subsequent revision process mean live data-sharing is still some way off.

For European firms with Canadian operations or ambitions, the framework's scope is worth watching. Open Finance Network Canada has flagged the potential for the regime to extend beyond banking into insurance, which would make it broader than most European implementations at launch.

*Sources: [Proposed Consumer-Driven Banking Regulations Released for Comment](https://www.mondaq.com/canada/financial-services/1812276/proposed-consumer-driven-banking-regulations-released-for-comment) — Mondaq (Fasken) | [Financial data sharing in Canada closer to reality](https://insurance-portal.ca/article/financial-data-sharing-in-canada-closer-to-reality/) — Insurance Portal | [Open Banking Milestone: Draft Consumer-Driven Banking Regulations Released](https://www.mondaq.com/canada/financial-services/1812418/open-banking-milestone-draft-consumer-driven-banking-regulations-released) — Mondaq (Fasken)*
